kept.claim: Revenue rose 22% from a year earlier to about $1.23 billion for the quarter. Management says subscription revenue grew mainly because of new customers and existing customers buying more sensors and modules.

Gross margin was 75.1% for the quarter, up 0.3 percentage points from a year earlier. Subscription cost of revenue still grew, driven mainly by higher cloud hosting costs, employee-related expenses from a larger average headcount and depreciation of data center equipment.

Total deferred revenue reached about $4.06 billion, up 27% from a year earlier. The filing explains that most subscription customers are invoiced at the start of their term, so these prepayments are recorded as deferred revenue and recognized as revenue later.

Operating cash flow was about $398 million for the quarter, up 22% from a year earlier, even though the company reported a net loss. For the year to date, the filing attributes operating cash to non-cash charges such as stock-based compensation and to an increase in deferred revenue.
